application.cover_letter_markdown:
Oulu has been on my radar since I first read about the city's RF and photonics engineering cluster while still at Yangtze Delta Institute of Technology. When I moved here in January to join Boreal Photonics, what I found matched the reading — a genuine concentration of wireless, space-systems, and optical-instrument expertise, all within a few kilometres. Kaikuvaara's work on remote-sensing instrument electronics sits at the centre of that cluster, and the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role is what prompted this application.

The part of my background most relevant to this role does not appear on my CV, because it predates my current position. During my final-year research at YDIT, I designed and simulated a 16-element uniform linear array beamformer for a phased-array weather radar prototype. The work involved both conventional delay-and-sum and Capon beamforming, implemented in MATLAB and validated against measured channel data from a test array in the university's radar laboratory. That project ran for seven months and the resulting beamforming weights and calibration routine stayed in use by the lab group after I left.

At Boreal I have also had my first real experience of technical leadership. The calibration-pipeline project described in my CV was effectively mine to run: I scoped the work, assigned modules to one intern and one recently hired engineer, reviewed their code, and was accountable for the delivery timeline. It was not a formal management title, but it was genuine responsibility for other people's work, and I found I liked it.

I hold a Finnish residence permit (type B, specialist) and have already submitted my application for the permanent A permit, which Boreal supports. I am legally authorised to work in Finland and across the EU.

Two things I want to be upfront about: I studied Kalman filtering and estimation theory as part of my signal processing coursework and have applied the concepts in simulation exercises, though not yet in a shipped system. I also have some awareness of satellite and airborne platform constraints from colleagues who work on space-qualified hardware, but I have not personally worked on a flight instrument programme.

I am in Oulu already and am not going anywhere. This is the engineering community I chose, and Kaikuvaara is doing the work I want to grow into.

Valentina Nwosu

application.cover_letter_markdown:
After thirteen years at Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems I have a fairly clear picture of what I am good at and what I want to do next. My work has been almost entirely on wideband receiver processing chains — designing the algorithms, writing the FPGA host code, building the test infrastructure around it. It has been satisfying work and I am proud of the publications that came out of it. But the receiver processing side is mature in our product line now, and the projects coming through are incremental rather than new. I am looking for a role where the signal processing problems are harder and the engineering is closer to the physics.

Kaikuvaara's instrument work involves the kind of phased-array and beamforming problems I have been drawn to for a while — that is what prompted the hobby demonstrator I describe in my CV, trying to get my hands on the problem space in a way my day-to-day receiver work did not offer. The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role reads like work I have been circling for years, and Oulu's focused engineering community is somewhere I could go deep on a problem rather than remaining a generalist.

My career at Tuulenkaari has been fairly linear — joined after finishing my physics MSc, grew into the senior role I hold now, built a team-lead track record along the way — but two things on my CV might look unusual. First, the beamforming demonstrator. It is a personal project with no institutional backing, and I realise that is an odd thing to include on an application for a senior engineering position. I put it in because it is the closest I have to hands-on phased-array work, and I wanted to be straightforward about what that experience is and what its limits are. It works, but it is four elements and electrical tape, not production hardware. Second, my embedded C/C++ and Python work both sit under "Projects" rather than the main job description. That is a presentational choice — they are core parts of my role at Tuulenkaari, but I found it clearer to describe them as discrete deliverables with their own scope.

What I would bring: deep familiarity with the full signal path from the RF front end to processed output, a decade of production C++ and Python in a real engineering team, and the discipline of someone who has maintained his own test frameworks long enough to know what "maintainable" actually means in practice. I have looked into what Kaikuvaara builds and I have a reasonable sense of where your technical challenges sit.

I am ready to relocate and can start with a standard notice period.

Henrik Andersson

application.cover_letter_markdown:
I have wanted to work on remote-sensing instruments since my undergraduate days at Rheinmark TU Aachen, when a guest lecture on SAR image formation made something click — the signal processing problems behind spaceborne and airborne radar are the most technically demanding in the field, and they come with consequences that ordinary communications work does not. If you get the beamforming wrong on a maritime radar, a ship track drops out. If you get it wrong on an instrument already in orbit, the mission data is gone. That asymmetry is what drew me to this domain, and it is what draws me to Kaikuvaara.

My MSc in Electrical Engineering from Rheinmark TU Aachen is where the technical foundations were laid. The thesis was on space-time adaptive processing for ground-based radar arrays — a topic I chose specifically because it sits at the intersection of array signal processing, statistical estimation, and real-time implementation, all of which turned out to be exactly what I needed at Nordkom. The coursework in electromagnetic field theory, stochastic signal processing, and digital communications that supported the thesis has remained directly relevant to my daily work. I bring this up because the alignment between what I studied and what your posting describes is unusually close.

My CV covers the specifics of my work at Nordkom over the past three years: phased-array beamforming for the maritime radar product, RF element-level characterisation, Kalman filter design for multi-target tracking, and embedded DSP implementation on the TI C6678. What the CV does not capture well is scope. Over the past year especially, I have become the person colleagues come to when a problem crosses subsystem boundaries, and I have had the chance to coordinate small groups of engineers working across the processing chain. I am comfortable with technical leadership and it is something I want to do formally in my next role.

Regarding Oulu: my partner is from Kempele, and we have been planning a move north for over a year. I have visited Oulu several times and have a sense of the city and the engineering community there. The timing is right. I am a Finnish citizen and hold full EU work authorisation.

The instruments Kaikuvaara builds — the SAR payloads, the scatterometer electronics — are exactly the systems I have spent the last several years learning to think about from a different vantage point at Nordkom. Paivi Koskinen

Phased-array signal processing for Fenno's FRT-400 ground-surveillance radar. - Based in Oulu (Fenno's main site); relocated here from Tampere when I first joined in 2017.

Wrote the matched-filter and pulse-compression module in C++ for the Zynq UltraScale+ SoC used in the FRT-500 prototype. Handles real-time sample ingestion via AXI DMA, performs complex matched filtering on the ARM core, and outputs detection data to the downstream tracker. In active use since 2023.

**Extended Kalman filter for manoeuvring-target tracking**
Designed and implemented an extended Kalman filter (EKF) that tracks multiple manoeuvring targets using a coordinated-turn motion model. Part of the radar's real-time processing chain. application.cover_letter_markdown:
My career at Fenno Radar Technologies has been the kind of slow build that does not look dramatic from the outside but adds up to something solid. I joined in 2017 straight from Tammerkoski University, took a year off in 2019 to travel — something I had been putting off since my undergraduate years — and came back to a role with more scope than the one I had left. Seven years of ground-surveillance radar work later, I am looking for what comes next.

Kaikuvaara is that, or I think it could be. What attracts me is the instrument work specifically — the requirement profile for this role reads like a natural extension of what I have been doing at Fenno, but on harder problems and with a wider technical scope. At Fenno the product line is mature. The beamforming architecture is settled, the tracking algorithms perform well in the field, the RF calibration is a routine I could run in my sleep. That stability is good for customers, but it is not what I need for my own development. I want problems that push me.

On the publications side, since it may not be obvious from my CV: I have a paper in ISRT Radar, Sonar & Navigation (2022, "Coordinated-turn EKF design for multi-target tracking in dense clutter", Reddy and Virtanen) that grew out of the tracker work at Fenno. A single publication, not a prolific record, but the work behind it was genuine and it went through proper peer review. I have also given two conference presentations at the Baltic Radar Conference, both in English, which leads to the language point — English has been my working language for most of my professional life. At Fenno all specifications, design reviews, and technical discussions are conducted in English because the team includes engineers from four countries. My thesis at Tampere was written and defended in English. I do not think of English as a foreign language any more; it is just the language I work in.

The sabbatical year is exactly what it looks like. I travelled in South America and Southeast Asia, did no engineering, and came back ready. It was the right decision and I would make it again.

I have been at Fenno long enough to know what I am good at and where I want to take my career. The signal processing work at Kaikuvaara — the complexity, the instrument-level integration, the fact that you build things that get deployed into demanding environments with real consequences — is where I want to be next.

Chidinma Reddy

Tiina Rantanen

tiina.rantanen@aurinko-avionics.example | Oulu

Experience

Signal Processing Engineer — Aurinko Avionics, Oulu
2004 – present

Processing and analysis of sensor data for Aurinko's airborne instrument product line. Work spans algorithm development, signal-chain integration, and collaboration with the hardware team on instrument-level verification.

- English is the engineering working language at Aurinko; all technical documents, specifications, and design reviews are conducted in English.
- Joined Aurinko when the company was still in Espoo; relocated to Oulu with the company in 2011 and have been based here since.

Projects

Engine-control-unit embedded software (secondment to Lohtaja, 2014–2015)
Spent fourteen months on secondment to Lohtaja's marine engine division, developing engine-control-unit embedded software in C for a dual-fuel engine controller. The work involved reading sensor channels (pressure, temperature, vibration) at a fixed 10 kHz sample rate, running a state machine for fuel-switching decisions, and meeting hard real-time constraints on an ARM Cortex-M4. Outside my usual domain, but the embedded firmware skills carried over directly.

GLACIOS-3 readout chain signal conditioning
Developed the signal-conditioning firmware for Aurinko's contribution to the GLACIOS-3 lidar instrument — a satellite payload that has been in orbit since 2022. Responsible for the digital filtering and decimation stage that processes raw ADC output from the detector front end. Work included environmental qualification testing and review against EORA SPEQ standards.

Airborne microwave radiometer ground-segment processing
Designed the ground-segment processing pipeline for data from an airborne microwave radiometer flown on a modified King Air B200. The pipeline performs channel calibration, antenna-pattern correction, and georeferencing. This project drew directly on the physics background from my CRIT degree — the radiometric calibration mathematics is fundamentally measurement physics.

Aurelia calibration campaign
Participated as a contributing engineer in the Aurelia "CalVal-Ice" field campaign (2019–2020), a calibration exercise for radiometer instruments. The project required verified EU work authorisation; I hold Finnish citizenship.

Education

CRIT, Cambridge, Massachusetts
MSc Physics, 2003

Skills

MATLAB, Simulink, VHDL
Linux, bash, Make
Oscilloscopes, logic analysers
application.cover_letter_markdown:
The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara is a close match for the work I have been doing at Aurinko Avionics for the past twenty-two years. I know remote-sensing instruments. I have built firmware that is currently in orbit and data-processing chains for airborne radiometers that have flown hundreds of hours of science missions. Kaikuvaara's focus on SAR and scatterometer payload electronics is the area of this domain I would most want to deepen.

Three things that may not be obvious from my CV, because they are woven into larger projects rather than listed as separate skills:

Phased-array signal processing. At Aurinko I designed the beamforming firmware for a 32-element L-band receive array used in an airborne SAR demonstrator (2017–2019). The work involved implementing a conventional delay-and-sum beamformer with per-element phase and amplitude correction, integrated into the real-time processing chain on the instrument's FPGA host processor.

Production Python. I wrote and maintain the calibration-data management system for Aurinko's instrument test laboratory — roughly 8,000 lines of Python, fully tested, with a PostgreSQL backend and a Flask-based internal web interface. In production since 2018, used daily by the entire test team.

RF measurement. I spent two years (2020–2022) doing hands-on RF characterisation of the L-band front end for the SAR demonstrator: S-parameter measurements on a Keysight PNA-L, antenna-pattern sweeps in Aurinko's compact range, and systematic calibration of the receive chain's gain and noise figure across temperature.

These are not side skills. They are central to what I do. I listed the engine-control firmware and the satellite and airborne projects on my CV because those were the largest discrete pieces of work, but the beamforming, the Python tooling, and the RF bench work are equally part of my day-to-day.

Tiina Rantanen
